opti.brief: She can't leave Canvas, so you go. Scout a court building in VR and send her one short video.
opti.desk: No headset? Use my desk. Play the game, then write 2 sentences for your teacher.

vr.look: This map is the U.S. Supreme Court. Florida's Supreme Court, in Tallahassee, has 7 justices. Courts are the judicial branch: they decide what laws mean.

place.html: The rules come first: Florida's constitution splits the work into three branches.
place.cap: Page 1 of Florida's first constitution, 1838. State Archives of Florida.

say: The judicial branch's job is to ___.

steps.title: Get ready
steps.html:
@PLACE@

In your video, you say these 2 sentences:

@SAY@

Practice now. Say both before the timer ends.

@TIMER@

In VR, this page is on the Canvas tab.

steps.title: Go in
steps.html:
🔗 First time only: connect Canvas at xr.optimaed.com. See Having trouble in VR? below.

Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Supreme in Filter environments. Click Supreme Court, then Begin Solo.

steps.title: Scout the court
steps.html: Move with the thumbstick. Look at the front of the building, the steps and the tall columns. Stop where you can see all of them.

steps.title: Record your video and send it
steps.html:
Open your menu, click Library, then Camera. Fit the building in the tablet. Click Record video, say your 2 sentences, and click it again to stop.

On the Canvas tab, pick @CANVAS@. Click Choose from My Files, pick your video, click Use this file, then Submit to Canvas. Look for the green Submitted tag.

🔁 To fix it, send a new video.

steps.title: Check and leave
steps.html: Press the Meta button, then click Quit. Check that your video is in the Canvas assignment. Not there? See Having trouble in VR?

extra.html: Turn slowly while you record, so your teacher sees how big the building is.

vr.full: One video, 30 seconds or less, showing the place while you say both sentences.

studio.title: Spin the Branches
studio.look: A wheel with six parts of Florida's government. Each one asks a question.
studio.do: Spin the wheel. Answer the question it lands on. Keep going until all six are done.

game.miss: Not quite. Think about what that branch does.
game.done: Six for six! Power is shared, so no one person has too much.

slices.name: Legislature
slices.q: What does the Florida Legislature do?
slices.ok: Yes! The Legislature makes the laws.

slices.name: Governor
slices.q: What can the governor do with a bill?
slices.ok: Yes! Sign it, or veto it, which means reject it.

slices.name: Two chambers
slices.q: What are the two chambers of the Legislature?

slices.name: Override
slices.q: How can a vetoed bill still become law?
options: Two-thirds of both chambers vote for it again

slices.name: Sharing power
slices.q: Why split the work into three branches?
options: So no one person or group gets too much control
